title: Session 5: Database Administration, Storage, Filegroups, and Snapshots — SQL Server

questions.questionText: Which of the following is a complete administration utility for SQL Server?
questions.correctAnswer: SQL Server Management Studio (SSMS)
questions.explanation: SQL Server Management Studio (SSMS) is a complete administrative and management graphical utility for SQL Server.

questions.questionText: Users are NOT allowed to directly update information in which of the following?
options: System tables, system stored procedures, and catalog views
questions.correctAnswer: System tables, system stored procedures, and catalog views
questions.explanation: Users are prevented from directly modifying system tables, system stored procedures, and catalog views to protect database integrity.

questions.questionText: Which API includes complete functionality for administering SQL Server in applications?
questions.correctAnswer: SQL Server Management Objects (SQL-SMO)
questions.explanation: SQL Server Management Objects (SQL-SMO) is the programmatic object model that exposes complete administration functionality for SQL Server.

questions.questionText: Which of these is required information to create a user-defined database?
options: Only the name of the database
Name, owner, size, and files and filegroups of the database
questions.correctAnswer: Name, owner, size, and files and filegroups of the database
questions.explanation: Creating a user-defined database requires identifying the name, owner, initial size, collation, and physical files and filegroups.

questions.questionText: The purpose of user-defined databases is to store ______.
questions.correctAnswer: user data
questions.explanation: User-defined databases are created specifically to store user and application data, separate from system metadata.

questions.questionText: In the CREATE DATABASE syntax, which clause indicates the disk files used to store the database log?
questions.correctAnswer: LOG ON
questions.explanation: The LOG ON clause defines the physical disk files allocated for recording the transaction log.

questions.questionText: In the CREATE DATABASE syntax, the ON clause indicates ______.
options: the disk files used to store the log
the disk files used to store the data sections of the database
questions.correctAnswer: the disk files used to store the data sections of the database
questions.explanation: The ON clause in CREATE DATABASE designates the disk files used to store the data sections of the database.

questions.questionText: What does the COLLATE clause define in CREATE DATABASE?
options: The default collation (rules for comparing and sorting character data) for the database
The size of the log file
questions.correctAnswer: The default collation (rules for comparing and sorting character data) for the database
questions.explanation: The COLLATE clause specifies the database default collation, determining how character data is sorted and compared.

questions.questionText: A collation defines rules for ______.
options: comparing and sorting character data based on a particular language and locale
questions.correctAnswer: comparing and sorting character data based on a particular language and locale
questions.explanation: A collation provides the rules for comparing and sorting character data according to language, culture, case, and accent sensitivity.

questions.questionText: Which is the correct syntax to create a database with a primary file and log file?
options: CREATE DATABASE [Customer_DB] ON PRIMARY (NAME='Customer_DB', FILENAME='...Customer_DB.mdf') LOG ON (...)
questions.correctAnswer: CREATE DATABASE [Customer_DB] ON PRIMARY (NAME='Customer_DB', FILENAME='...Customer_DB.mdf') LOG ON (...)
questions.explanation: The standard SQL Server syntax is CREATE DATABASE [db_name] ON PRIMARY (NAME=..., FILENAME=...) LOG ON (...).

questions.questionText: Which file extension is recommended for the primary database file?
questions.correctAnswer: .mdf
questions.explanation: Microsoft recommends .mdf (Master Data File) as the file extension for primary data files.

questions.questionText: Which file extension is recommended for the transaction log file?
questions.correctAnswer: .ldf
questions.explanation: The recommended file extension for SQL Server transaction log files is .ldf (Log Data File).

questions.questionText: Which file extension is recommended for secondary data files?
questions.correctAnswer: .ndf
questions.explanation: Secondary data files use the recommended file extension .ndf.

questions.questionText: MDF stands for ______.
questions.correctAnswer: Master Database File
questions.explanation: MDF stands for Master Database File (also known as Master Data File).

questions.questionText: Does SQL Server enforce the .mdf, .ndf, and .ldf file name extensions?
options: No, they are only recommended to help identify the use of the file
Only for databases created using SSMS
questions.correctAnswer: No, they are only recommended to help identify the use of the file
questions.explanation: SQL Server does not enforce file extensions; .mdf, .ndf, and .ldf are recommended conventions to clarify file roles.

questions.questionText: Which statement is used to modify an existing database?
questions.correctAnswer: ALTER DATABASE
questions.explanation: The ALTER DATABASE statement is used to modify the configuration, files, or properties of an existing database.

questions.questionText: Which is the correct statement to rename the database Customer_DB to CUST_DB?
options: ALTER DATABASE Customer_DB MODIFY NAME = CUST_DB
UPDATE DATABASE Customer_DB SET NAME = CUST_DB
questions.correctAnswer: ALTER DATABASE Customer_DB MODIFY NAME = CUST_DB
questions.explanation: The syntax to rename a database in SQL Server is ALTER DATABASE Customer_DB MODIFY NAME = CUST_DB.

questions.questionText: Which of the following can be performed using ALTER DATABASE?
options: Add or modify files and filegroups, set database options, rename, and change collation
questions.correctAnswer: Add or modify files and filegroups, set database options, rename, and change collation
questions.explanation: ALTER DATABASE can add or modify files and filegroups, configure options, rename the database, and modify collation.

questions.questionText: Which system stored procedure is used to change the ownership of a database?
questions.correctAnswer: sp_changedbowner
questions.explanation: The sp_changedbowner system stored procedure changes the ownership of a database.

questions.questionText: After sp_changedbowner is executed, the new owner is known as the ______ user inside the database.
questions.correctAnswer: dbo
questions.explanation: Inside the database, the database owner is mapped to the dbo user.

questions.questionText: The ownership of which of these databases CANNOT be changed?
options: master, model, and tempdb system databases
questions.correctAnswer: master, model, and tempdb system databases
questions.explanation: The ownership of system databases (master, model, tempdb) cannot be changed.

questions.questionText: Which of these is NOT a database option type supported by SQL Server 2019?
questions.correctAnswer: Network options
questions.explanation: Network options are configured at the SQL Server instance/protocol level, not as database options.

questions.questionText: Which database option type controls recovery models of a database?
questions.correctAnswer: Recovery options
questions.explanation: Recovery options control the recovery model (FULL, BULK_LOGGED, SIMPLE) and page verification.

questions.questionText: Which database option type controls the online/offline state and user connectivity?
questions.correctAnswer: State options
questions.explanation: State options govern the state of the database (ONLINE, OFFLINE, EMERGENCY) and access modes (SINGLE_USER, RESTRICTED_USER, MULTI_USER).

questions.questionText: Database options are set using which clause of the ALTER DATABASE statement?
questions.correctAnswer: SET
questions.explanation: Database options are configured using the SET clause, e.g., ALTER DATABASE database_name SET option_name ON|OFF.

questions.questionText: Server-wide settings in SQL Server are set using ______.
options: the sp_configure system stored procedure or SSMS
questions.correctAnswer: the sp_configure system stored procedure or SSMS
questions.explanation: Server-level configuration options are managed using the sp_configure system stored procedure or Server Properties in SSMS.

questions.questionText: What does setting the AUTO_SHRINK option to ON do?
options: Shrinks the database that has free space
questions.correctAnswer: Shrinks the database that has free space
questions.explanation: When AUTO_SHRINK is ON, SQL Server periodically shrinks database files that contain unused free space.

questions.questionText: In SQL Server, data files are subdivided into ______ for the sake of performance.
questions.correctAnswer: filegroups
questions.explanation: Data files are grouped into filegroups to manage storage allocation, separation, and parallel disk I/O performance.

questions.questionText: Where are all system tables placed?
questions.correctAnswer: Inside the primary filegroup
questions.explanation: All system tables and catalog metadata are placed in the primary filegroup.

questions.questionText: What is the maximum number of filegroups that can be created for each database?
questions.explanation: SQL Server allows a maximum of 32,767 filegroups per database.

questions.questionText: Which statement about filegroups is correct?
options: Transaction log files must belong to the primary filegroup
Filegroups can contain only data files; transaction log files cannot belong to a filegroup
Filegroups can contain only log files
A filegroup can contain only one file
questions.correctAnswer: Filegroups can contain only data files; transaction log files cannot belong to a filegroup
questions.explanation: Filegroups are exclusively used for data files (.mdf and .ndf); transaction log files (.ldf) are never part of a filegroup.

questions.questionText: Which statement about a file and filegroups is correct?
options: A file cannot be a member of more than one filegroup at the same time
A file can belong to any number of filegroups
A file can belong to a maximum of two filegroups
A log file can belong to a user-defined filegroup
questions.correctAnswer: A file cannot be a member of more than one filegroup at the same time
questions.explanation: In SQL Server, a specific data file can belong to only one filegroup at any time.

questions.questionText: Can a file be moved to a different filegroup after it has been added to the database?
options: Yes, but only for log files
No, files cannot be moved to a different filegroup once added
questions.correctAnswer: No, files cannot be moved to a different filegroup once added
questions.explanation: Once a file is created and associated with a filegroup, it cannot be reassigned or moved to another filegroup.

questions.questionText: Which statement adds a filegroup named FG_ReadOnly to the existing database CUST_DB?
options: ALTER DATABASE CUST_DB CREATE FILEGROUP FG_ReadOnly
ALTER DATABASE CUST_DB ADD FILEGROUP FG_ReadOnly
UPDATE DATABASE CUST_DB ADD FILEGROUP FG_ReadOnly
questions.correctAnswer: ALTER DATABASE CUST_DB ADD FILEGROUP FG_ReadOnly
questions.explanation: The syntax to add a filegroup is ALTER DATABASE [dbname] ADD FILEGROUP [filegroup_name].

questions.questionText: What is required to make a filegroup the default filegroup?
options: It must contain the transaction log
It must contain at least one file
questions.correctAnswer: It must contain at least one file
questions.explanation: To be designated as the default filegroup, it must not be empty (must contain at least one file).

questions.questionText: Which statement makes the filegroup FG_ReadOnly the default filegroup?
options: ALTER DATABASE CUST_DB MODIFY FILEGROUP FG_ReadOnly DEFAULT
ALTER DATABASE CUST_DB SET DEFAULT FILEGROUP FG_ReadOnly
questions.correctAnswer: ALTER DATABASE CUST_DB MODIFY FILEGROUP FG_ReadOnly DEFAULT
questions.explanation: The statement ALTER DATABASE CUST_DB MODIFY FILEGROUP FG_ReadOnly DEFAULT designates FG_ReadOnly as the default filegroup.

questions.questionText: What does the transaction log in SQL Server record?
options: All transactions and the database modifications made by each transaction
questions.correctAnswer: All transactions and the database modifications made by each transaction
questions.explanation: The transaction log records all transactions and data modifications to ensure data integrity and facilitate recovery.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is a clause used to add a transaction log file to an existing database?
questions.correctAnswer: ADD LOG FILE
questions.explanation: The ADD LOG FILE clause of ALTER DATABASE is used to add an additional transaction log file.

questions.questionText: Which Transact-SQL statement is used to delete a database?
questions.correctAnswer: DROP DATABASE
questions.explanation: The DROP DATABASE statement deletes one or more user-defined databases or snapshots.

questions.questionText: What should be done before dropping a database?
options: The log file should be deleted
A full backup of the database should be taken
A snapshot should be set as default
questions.correctAnswer: A full backup of the database should be taken
questions.explanation: A full backup should always be taken before dropping a database so that data can be recovered if needed.

questions.questionText: A deleted database can be re-created only by ______.
questions.correctAnswer: restoring a backup
questions.explanation: Because DROP DATABASE removes the physical files from disk, the database can only be re-created by restoring from a backup.

questions.questionText: Which of these statements about a database snapshot is true?
options: It provides a read-write copy of the database
It can be created only using SSMS
It can be backed up like a normal database
It provides a read-only, static view of a SQL Server database
questions.correctAnswer: It provides a read-only, static view of a SQL Server database
questions.explanation: A database snapshot provides a read-only, static, point-in-time view of a SQL Server source database.

questions.questionText: How can a database snapshot be created?
options: Using Transact-SQL only; SSMS does not support it
questions.correctAnswer: Using Transact-SQL only; SSMS does not support it
questions.explanation: SQL Server Management Studio does not support creating snapshots through its graphical interface; they must be created using T-SQL.

questions.questionText: Which of these is an advantage of database snapshots?
options: Snapshot backups can be created easily
New users can be granted access to snapshot data
Snapshots can be located on any server
When queried, there is no deterioration of server performance
questions.correctAnswer: When queried, there is no deterioration of server performance
questions.explanation: Snapshots provide reporting views that isolate reads from live write locks, helping prevent query contention and server performance deterioration on live data.

questions.questionText: Which of these is a disadvantage of database snapshots?
options: A snapshot backup cannot be created
They take a long time to create
questions.correctAnswer: A snapshot backup cannot be created
questions.explanation: A key limitation of database snapshots is that SQL Server does not support taking backups of snapshot databases.

questions.questionText: Which of these is a disadvantage of database snapshots?
options: A snapshot must exist on the same database server as the source database
questions.correctAnswer: A snapshot must exist on the same database server as the source database
questions.explanation: Database snapshots are tied directly to their source database and must reside on the exact same SQL Server instance.

questions.questionText: Which clause is used in CREATE DATABASE to create a database snapshot?
questions.correctAnswer: AS SNAPSHOT OF
questions.explanation: The AS SNAPSHOT OF clause in the CREATE DATABASE statement indicates the source database for the snapshot.

questions.questionText: In a database snapshot, if a user makes a mistake in the source database, the source database can be ______.
options: reverted to the state when the snapshot was created
questions.correctAnswer: reverted to the state when the snapshot was created
questions.explanation: The source database can be restored/reverted back to the snapshot's point in time, discarding errors made after the snapshot was taken.

questions.questionText: In the New Database dialog box in SSMS, how can the database collation be changed?
options: Select the Options page and choose a collation from the list
questions.correctAnswer: Select the Options page and choose a collation from the list
questions.explanation: In SSMS, the Collation setting is located on the Options page of the New Database dialog.

questions.questionText: In SSMS, where can a new filegroup be added while creating a database?
questions.correctAnswer: The Filegroups page
questions.explanation: In SSMS New Database dialog, the Filegroups page is where additional filegroups are defined.
